The statement’s core message—solid real activity, strong labor markets, and easing but still-elevated inflation—pairs with a restrictive hold at 5.25–5.50% and ongoing balance-sheet runoff. Read through the modern reaction-function lens of Clarida, Galí, and Gertler, this is consistent with a policy that responds to both the inflation and activity gaps while inflation remains above target. The emphasis on “greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2%” aligns with Svensson and Woodford’s forecast-targeting framework and the New Keynesian Phillips Curve’s focus on expectations; clear commitment helps contain average inflation bias and time-inconsistency risks. Given still-tight labor markets (Okun’s law implies limited slack) and the role of expectations in the NKPC, a cautious stance is warranted. Continued QT and an ample-floor system with interest on reserves at 5.4% work through money markets and the yield curve (consistent with term-structure insights such as Cochrane-Piazzesi) to keep overall financial conditions restrictive. Net tone: cautiously optimistic but still hawkish—improving balance of risks is positive, yet disinflation credibility remains the priority after the 2020 shift to average-inflation targeting.
